title: Accenture, Dragos, SANS Launch $10M Initiative to Defend Small US Utilities
description: Accenture, Dragos, and the SANS Institute have launched a $10 million initiative called the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation to help under-resourced small US utilities defend their operational technology (OT) environments. The first phase targets up to 500 water, electric, and natural gas utilities with annual revenues under $100 million, providing free security tools, equipment, deployment assistance, and training. The initiative aims to address challenges faced by small utilities such as limited funding, workforce shortages, and aging technology. Participants receive the Dragos Platform and related services, with Accenture managing setup and support, and SANS providing ICS/OT security training. This effort builds on Dragos's existing Community Defense Program and responds to recent attacks on US water systems. The program is intended to improve cyber resilience in critical infrastructure sectors serving millions of Americans.
aiSummary: The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation, a $10 million initiative by Accenture, Dragos, and the SANS Institute, targets small US utilities with less than $100 million in annual revenue to enhance their cybersecurity posture for operational technology environments. The program provides up to 500 utilities with free access to the Dragos Platform, deployment support from Accenture, and ICS/OT security training from SANS. It addresses the cybersecurity challenges faced by small utilities, including limited resources and workforce shortages, especially in rural and underserved areas. The initiative aims to strengthen defenses against adversaries targeting critical infrastructure, building on Dragos's prior Community Defense Program launched in 2023. This effort is a proactive measure to mitigate risks following recent attacks on US water systems.
aiImpact: This initiative aims to reduce the cybersecurity risk to small US utilities by providing them with advanced security tools, expertise, and training. By improving the security posture of these utilities, the program helps protect critical infrastructure that delivers essential services such as water, electricity, and natural gas to millions of Americans. The impact is primarily preventive, aiming to mitigate the threat posed by adversaries targeting operational technology environments in small utilities, which historically have limited capacity to defend themselves.
